@@ -0,0 +1,222 @@
+---
+on:
+  schedule: weekly on monday
+description: Checks whether the list of Copilot-accessible models in src/inspect/catalog.rs and prompts/create-ado-agentic-workflow.md is current; opens a PR when new models are available or old ones have been removed.
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: read
+  pull-requests: read
+  copilot-requests: write
+tools:
+  github:
+    toolsets: [default]
+network:
+  allowed: [defaults]
+safe-outputs:
+  threat-detection:
+    max-ai-credits: -1
+  create-pull-request:
+    title-prefix: "chore(deps): "
+    max: 1
+    allowed-files:
+      - src/inspect/catalog.rs
+      - prompts/create-ado-agentic-workflow.md
+  close-pull-request:
+    required-title-prefix: "chore(deps): update copilot model list"
+    target: "*"
+    max: 5
+  create-issue:
+    title-prefix: "[copilot-models] "
+    labels: [automation, dependencies]
+    max: 1
+  noop:
+max-ai-credits: -1
+max-daily-ai-credits: -1
+---
+
+# Copilot Model List Updater
+
+You are a dependency maintenance bot for the **ado-aw** project — a Rust CLI
+compiler that transforms markdown agent definitions into Azure DevOps pipeline
+YAML.
+
+## Your Task
+
+Check whether the list of Copilot-accessible models kept in two files is still
+current, and open a PR to update it when it is not.
+
+The two files you are responsible for:
+
+| File | What to update |
+|------|----------------|
+| `src/inspect/catalog.rs` | string literals in the `models()` function |
+| `prompts/create-ado-agentic-workflow.md` | model table in "Step 2 — Engine" |
+
+---
+
+## Step 1 — Fetch Available Models
+
+Use the GitHub API to list models that are accessible to GitHub Copilot:
+
+```
+GET /models
+```
+
+From the response, collect every model whose `vendor` (or `publisher`) is
+`anthropic` or `openai` **and** whose identifier the Copilot CLI `--model` flag
+accepts. The canonical identifier is the `id` (or `name`) field returned by the
+API. Record the full list as `api_models`.
+
+If the API call fails or returns an empty list, emit a `report-incomplete`
+safe output explaining what went wrong and stop — do not open a PR against a
+potentially stale snapshot.
+
+---
+
+## Step 2 — Read the Current Model List
+
+**From `src/inspect/catalog.rs`:**
+
+Read the file and locate the `models()` function. Extract every string literal
+inside that function. Call this set `catalog_models`. The first entry corresponds
+to `DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL`; read its current value from `src/engine.rs` (look for
+the line `pub const DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL: &str = "...";`).
+
+**From `prompts/create-ado-agentic-workflow.md`:**
+
+Read the file and locate the model table inside "Step 2 — Engine". Extract
+every model identifier from the table rows. Call this set `prompt_models`.
+
+The **current tracked set** is the union of `catalog_models` and
+`prompt_models`. The `DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL` string is always present in
+`catalog_models` as the first entry.
+
+---
+
+## Step 3 — Compare
+
+Compute:
+
+- **New models** (`new_models`): identifiers in `api_models` that are absent
+  from both `catalog_models` and `prompt_models`.
+- **Gone models** (`gone_models`): identifiers in the current tracked set that
+  are no longer in `api_models`, **excluding** the `DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL`
+  entry (never auto-remove the default).
+
+If both `new_models` and `gone_models` are empty, **stop** — everything is up
+to date. Emit a `noop` safe output with the message
+`"Copilot model list is current; no changes needed."` and exit.
+
+### Check for an existing open PR
+
+Search for open PRs whose titles start with
+`chore(deps): update copilot model list`.
+
+- If exactly one such PR is found **and** it would still produce the correct
+  result given the current `api_models` response (i.e. the diff it contains
+  already adds all `new_models` and removes all `gone_models`), **skip** —
+  an accurate PR is already open.
+- If a stale PR exists (the model list has changed since it was opened), emit a
+  `close-pull-request` safe output for it with a short comment explaining it is
+  superseded, then proceed to Step 4 to open a fresh one.
+
+---
+
+## Step 4 — Open an Update PR
+
+Edit exactly the two files described below and then open a PR.
+
+### 4a — Update `src/inspect/catalog.rs`
+
+Locate the `models()` function. Its body is a `vec![...]` literal.
+
+Rules:
+1. The very first entry **must** remain `DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL.to_string()` —
+   do not touch it.
+2. Add a `.to_string()` call for each identifier in `new_models`.
+3. Remove the `.to_string()` line for each identifier in `gone_models`.
+4. Keep all non-default entries sorted alphabetically by the string value.
+5. Do **not** change any other line in the file.
+
+Also update the comment immediately above the `vec![...]` if needed to keep it
+accurate (the comment currently says
+`// No KNOWN_MODELS registry exists yet; keep this list aligned with` —
+leave that wording intact).
+
+### 4b — Update `prompts/create-ado-agentic-workflow.md`
+
+Locate the model table inside "Step 2 — Engine" (search for the heading
+`### Step 2 — Engine` or the table row that contains the `DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL`
+value you read in Step 2).
+
+Rules:
+1. **Never** remove the row for the default model (whatever `DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL`
+   is set to in `src/engine.rs`).
+2. Add one row per model in `new_models`. Use the following guidance for the
+   "Use when" column:
+   - If the model name contains `opus` or `o1` or `o3`: "Highest reasoning
+     capability; use for the most complex tasks."
+   - If the model name contains `sonnet` or `gpt-4`: "Faster and cheaper than
+     Opus; good for moderate-complexity tasks."
+   - If the model name contains `haiku` or `gpt-3`: "Fastest and cheapest;
+     use for simple, well-scoped tasks."
+   - Otherwise: "Available model; review capabilities before choosing."
+3. Remove rows for models in `gone_models`.
+4. Keep the table rows sorted so that the default model is first, and the rest
+   are in alphabetical order by the model identifier column.
+5. Do **not** change any other part of the file.
+
+### 4c — Open the PR
+
+- **Title** (without the auto-prepended prefix):
+  `update copilot model list`
+  → published as `chore(deps): update copilot model list`
+
+- **Body**:
+
+```markdown
+## Copilot Model List Update
+
+Keeps the model catalog in `src/inspect/catalog.rs` and the recommended-model
+table in `prompts/create-ado-agentic-workflow.md` current with the models
+available via the GitHub Copilot API.
+
+### Changes
+
+**Added:**
+<bullet per new model — identifier and "Use when" description>
+
+**Removed:**
+<bullet per gone model, or "None." if empty>
+
+### Note on `DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL`
+
+This PR does **not** change the `DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL` constant in
+`src/engine.rs`. Choosing a new default is an
+opinionated, human decision that weighs stability, pricing, and capability
+trade-offs. If one of the newly added models is a strong candidate for the
+default, please update `src/engine.rs` and `prompts/create-ado-agentic-workflow.md`
+manually after review.
+
+### Source
+
+Models fetched from `GET /models` (GitHub Copilot API).
+See the [GitHub Models documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/github-models)
+for the full list of available models.
+
+---
+*This PR was opened automatically by the Copilot model list updater workflow.*
+```
+
+- **Base branch**: `main`
+
+---
+
+## What This Workflow Does NOT Change
+
+- `DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL` in `src/engine.rs` — requires a human decision.
+- Test fixture data (`src/audit/analyzers/otel.rs`,
+  `src/audit/render/console.rs`) — those strings record what a real past run
+  observed; they are intentionally historical and must not be auto-bumped.
+- Compiled `.lock.yml` files — those are generated from the `.md` source files
+  and must be recompiled separately via `gh aw compile`.

fix(workflows): repair the Copilot model list updater (#1760)

* fix(workflows): repair the Copilot model list updater

The weekly model updater has been silently doing nothing since it was added
in #1376. Three independent faults, all visible in its run logs:

1. Its data source no longer exists. Step 1 told the agent to call
   `GET /models`, but GitHub Models is being retired -- `models.github.ai`
   now returns HTTP 410 `github_models_retirement_brownout`, and both
   `GET /models` and `GET /catalog/models` return 404 on api.github.com.

2. The host was firewalled anyway. Every run shows the same AWF entry:

     blocked_domains: ["models.inference.ai.azure.com:443"]

   The workflow declares `network: allowed: [defaults]`, which does not
   include any GitHub Models host, so Step 1 could never have succeeded.

3. The agent had no shell. `tools:` granted only the github toolset, so it
   could not have run curl even against a reachable endpoint.

The result was a green run every week that checked nothing: turns=0,
tool_calls=null, and neither the `noop` nor the `report-incomplete` its own
prompt mandates -- while still burning ~32 AIC. gh-aw's own analyzer flagged
it as `overkill_for_agentic` with `evidence: turns=0 tool_types=0`.

Fixed by switching to the AWF `api-proxy` `/reflect` endpoint, which is what
gh-aw's own daily-model-inventory workflow uses for Copilot models. It is
reachable at http://api-proxy:10000/reflect from inside the agent sandbox, so
it needs no allowlist entry, and `apiProxy.enabled` is already true in our
compiled AWF config. It also reports the models this workflow's engine can
actually reach, rather than a public catalogue that may not match.

Also adds a `models_url` fallback for when `/reflect` returns null models, and
guards against acting on a malformed response: the agent must emit
`report-incomplete` rather than open a PR if the list is empty, and refuse
suspiciously large diffs (>20 additions, or removing more than half the list).

Separately, Step 2 read a model table in "Step 2 -- Engine" of
prompts/create-ado-agentic-workflow.md. That table no longer exists -- the
prompt was restructured and now defers to `DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL` in
src/engine.rs instead of hardcoding models. That file is dropped from the
tracked set and from `allowed-files`, leaving src/inspect/catalog.rs as the
single source this workflow maintains.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 475bd62b-12cb-41aa-88b6-39a3d75e3c50

* fix(workflows): allow full bash for the /reflect fetch

The per-command allow-list (curl/jq/mkdir/cat) denied the Step 1 fetch: the
/reflect snippet is a compound script and the sandbox rejects the whole call
unless every constituent -- including `set` and `printf` -- is allowed.

Verified against a real dispatch on this branch (run 30662916096), which
failed with "Permission denied and could not request permission from user"
and correctly emitted `report_incomplete` rather than exiting silently green
-- confirming the new failure-path guard works.

Matches gh-aw's own daily-model-inventory workflow and the five workflows in
this repo that already use `bash: ["*"]`. The security boundary is elsewhere:
the agent runs network-isolated with a read-only token, and every write goes
through safe-outputs restricted to src/inspect/catalog.rs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 475bd62b-12cb-41aa-88b6-39a3d75e3c50

* fix(workflows): correct model filtering and sanity guards

Verified against a real dispatch (run 30663481048). The /reflect fetch now
succeeds -- firewall reports blocked_requests: 0, and the agent wrote
/tmp/gh-aw/agent/reflect.json with 38 concrete Copilot model identifiers --
which exposed two bugs in the prompt logic.

First, the endpoint also advertises embedding and internal utility models
(text-embedding-3-small, text-embedding-ada-002, trajectory-compaction,
*-inference). Those are not valid `--model` values and must not be written
into the catalog, so they are now filtered out along with dated snapshot
duplicates such as gpt-4o-2024-05-13 where the undated name already exists.

Second, the ">20 new models is suspect" guard was wrong. src/inspect/catalog.rs
currently tracks just two entries, so a correct first sync legitimately adds
roughly thirty. The guard was written to catch malformed responses but instead
blocked the exact case the workflow exists to handle.

Replaced with a check that actually distinguishes malformed from stale: the
response must contain the current DEFAULT_COPILOT_MODEL. If the list does not
include the model this workflow's own engine runs on, it is not describing our
entitlements and the agent must report_incomplete. The "removing more than
half the list" guard is kept.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 475bd62b-12cb-41aa-88b6-39a3d75e3c50

* fix(workflows): stop the agent creating its own branch and commit

Run 30664463236 fetched and filtered the model list correctly, then failed at
the last step: create_pull_request returned "No commits were found" even though
the agent had made a valid commit on a branch it created itself.

That is the cause, not a contradiction. The create-pull-request safe output
builds the PR from uncommitted working-tree changes and does the branching,
committing and pushing itself with a token the agent never sees. By running
`git checkout -b` and `git commit`, the agent moved its changes out of the
working tree, leaving the safe output nothing to package.

Since bash ["*"] gives the agent git, the prompt now states explicitly that it
must edit the file and call the tool without branching or committing. This
matches clippy-fixer and bash-lint-auditor, which simply edit and hand off.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 475bd62b-12cb-41aa-88b6-39a3d75e3c50

* fix(workflows): drop the fetch-depth workaround

Reverts the `checkout: fetch-depth: 0` added in the previous commit. It was
masking a test artifact rather than fixing a defect, and the evidence does not
support it:

  - Six other workflows in this repo create pull requests (clippy-fixer,
    bash-lint-auditor, test-gap-finder, cyclomatic-complexity-reducer,
    test-reducer, docs-writer). None of them set fetch-depth.
  - gh-aw's own ~250 workflows use fetch-depth in workflow markdown zero times.
  - gh-aw's safe-outputs documentation never mentions it.

The real cause of "Git command failed / No commits were found" is how the run
was being triggered, not the workflow. Patch generation runs
`git merge-base origin/main <checkout-sha>`. I was testing via
workflow_dispatch on fix/copilot-models-updater, which had diverged from main
by 4 commits ahead and 14 behind, so under the default depth-1 clone there is
no common ancestor in the truncated history and merge-base exits 1.

On this workflow's actual trigger -- `schedule: weekly on monday`, which runs
on the default branch -- the checkout SHA is origin/main's tip, so the
merge-base is that same commit and resolves trivially. That is precisely why
the six sibling workflows have never needed this: they are all scheduled.

Keeping fetch-depth: 0 would have imposed a permanent full-history clone on a
workflow that edits one file, to work around a condition its real trigger
cannot produce.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 475bd62b-12cb-41aa-88b6-39a3d75e3c50
